_meta: Five candidate chunks retrieved for one query, to show why the top-k by relevance is often the wrong set to return. Each chunk has a relevance score to the query and a hidden 'aspect' (the sub-topic it covers). Chunks a1, a2, a3 all cover aspect A and are near-duplicates of each other (mutual similarity 0.9); chunks b1, b2 cover a different aspect B and are near-duplicates of each other but dissimilar to the A cluster (cross-similarity 0.1). a1/a2/a3 have slightly higher relevance than b1/b2, so taking the top 3 by relevance returns a1, a2, a3 -- three ways of saying the same thing, with aspect B entirely missing. Maximal Marginal Relevance instead balances relevance against redundancy, so it returns a diverse set that covers both aspects. similarity is the pairwise chunk-to-chunk similarity matrix aligned to ids; relevance and aspect are keyed by id; lambda trades relevance (1.0) against diversity (0.0); k is how many to return. Every selection and score is computed.
